# SK2182 — A type is identified by comparing its name to a string

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`x.GetType().Name == "Order"` binds a type by a string the compiler never checks, so a rename makes it silently false and any other assembly's `Order` makes it silently true.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, review it |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

The comparison looks like a type test and is a string test. Rename `Order` and every tool in the toolchain updates every reference except this one, which keeps compiling and starts returning `false` — the worst shape a defect can have, because the symptom is a branch that stops being taken rather than an exception anybody can trace. In the other direction `Type.Name` is not unique: any `Order` in any referenced assembly, in any namespace, matches. ⚠ **Nothing upstream implements this** — the SonarSource idea it comes from is an unspecified proposal — so the specification here is entirely Skala's, and the whole of it is the resolution test below.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
if (entity.GetType().Name == "Order") {
    Process(entity);
}
```

Write:

```csharp
if (entity.GetType() == typeof(Order)) {
    Process(entity);
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **The literal must name a type this compilation can already see, and that single condition is what separates the defect from the idiom.** Comparing a name is the *only* option for a type loaded reflectively, for a plugin an assembly deliberately does not reference, and for a shape crossing an assembly boundary — and in every one of those cases the name does not resolve here, so the rule is silent. A `Name` comparison resolves through the compilation's own declarations; a `FullName` comparison resolves through metadata as well, because a fully-qualified name that resolves is a type the file could have named outright. ⚠ **`AssemblyQualifiedName` is never reported.** It carries a version, a culture and a public key token, so a comparison against it is a deliberate statement about *which build* of a type this is, and `typeof(T)` does not say that. `Name`, `FullName` and `AssemblyQualifiedName` are three different questions and only two of them have a symbol-based answer. ⚠ **The receiver must be a `GetType()` call.** `t.Name == "Order"` on a `Type` variable has no `typeof` rewrite — the subject is a `Type`, not an instance — and is declined with a fixture rather than reported without a fix. ⚠ **The fix is `GetType() == typeof(T)` and never `is T`.** A name comparison is exact and `is` is not: rewriting to `is Order` would start matching every subclass, which is a behaviour change the string comparison never had. The replacement type is written short where that name binds to that type at the call site and fully qualified where it does not, so the edit compiles in a file with no matching `using`. `fixIsSafe: false`: the finding is about what the code does, so the edit changes it. Generated code is excluded.

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2182.severity`
